analysis:
The PR changes a single documentation line, docs/architecture/inference.md line 1846 (the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table). It now says stop strings are matched via `StopHoldback`. For GPT-OSS, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` limits matching to the Harmony `final` message, so analysis and tool-call frames never match, and the reported stop sequence replays the same scope. The change is prose only, with no code, config or deployment changes in this diff, so I found no new attack surface or security regression.

The text describes a behavioral constraint rather than a security control. Stop-string matching is scoped to the final channel, which reduces the chance that a consumer-supplied stop string truncates reasoning or tool-call frames. It touches no encryption, attestation, authorization, key custody or cache-storage behavior (A-001, A-003, T-041, T-008). The statement is relevant to TB-002 and TB-007 output integrity only indirectly. The other changed-adjacent text in units 6 and 7 (MTP, prefix cache, JSON constraints, MiMo) is unchanged context. I did not independently verify the claim against the Swift source (`ModelEOSPolicy`, `StopHoldback`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`), since those files are not supplied. The documentation matches the described design, but whether the implementation matches it is an unverified contract and belongs to whoever reviews the corresponding code change. The T-041 prefix-cache posture text in the surrounding doc is unchanged, and the sampler is still stated not to be part of cache identity.
